blocks.text: Imagine a world where computers couldn't remember anything. How would they function? Sequential circuits are the key to memory in digital systems.

blocks.markdown: In digital logic, circuits are broadly classified into two categories: combinational and sequential. Combinational circuits produce outputs based solely on the current inputs. In contrast, sequential circuits have memory and their outputs depend on both current inputs and past states.

blocks.title: Combinational Logic
blocks.text: A type of digital logic circuit whose output is a pure function of the present input only.

blocks.title: Sequential Logic
blocks.text: A type of digital logic circuit whose output depends on the current input and the history of past inputs.

blocks.markdown: The fundamental building block of sequential circuits is the flip-flop. A flip-flop can store a single bit of data and is controlled by a clock signal. The most common type is the D (Data) flip-flop.

blocks.title: D Flip-Flop
blocks.text: A digital storage element that captures the value of the D-input at a particular portion of the clock cycle (usually the rising or falling edge) and holds this value until the next clock cycle.

blocks.caption: The output Q of a D flip-flop at the next clock edge is equal to the input D at the current clock edge.

blocks.title: Understanding a D Flip-Flop
blocks.prompt: Consider a D flip-flop with a clock signal. If the D input is 1 when the clock edge occurs, what will be the output Q after the clock edge?

steps.text: Identify the input D at the clock edge.
Apply the D flip-flop rule: the output Q after the clock edge is equal to the input D at the clock edge.

blocks.answer: The output Q will be 1 after the clock edge.

blocks.markdown: The clock period in a sequential circuit is crucial. It must be long enough to allow signals to propagate through the longest combinational path between flip-flops. This ensures that data is stable and correctly captured at each clock edge.

blocks.title: Clock Period
blocks.text: The clock period must be greater than the propagation delay of the longest combinational path to ensure reliable operation.

blocks.title: Calculating Clock Period
blocks.prompt: A sequential circuit has a longest combinational path delay of 10 ns. What is the minimum clock period required for reliable operation?

steps.text: Identify the longest combinational path delay.
The clock period must be greater than this delay.

blocks.answer: The minimum clock period required is greater than 10 ns.

blocks.caption: Comparison of Combinational and Sequential Logic

points: Combinational logic depends only on current inputs, while sequential logic depends on current inputs and past states.
A D flip-flop stores a bit by capturing the D input at a clock edge.
The clock period must exceed the longest combinational path delay for reliable operation.
